metaDescription: Six Sharp countertop microwaves compared across 0.7 to 2.2 cubic feet, with inverter power, sensor cooking and carousel tray sizes for each kitchen.
expertTake: The Sharp SMC1464KS is the best Sharp pick because inverter power, a 1.4 cubic foot cavity and two-stage cooking cover defrosting and daily reheating well. The SMC0962KS is the value choice for small kitchens. Anyone who wants the biggest cavity should compare the SMC2266KS against the counter depth it demands.
introParagraphs: This maker sells a tidy ladder of countertop microwaves, from a compact 0.7 cubic foot oven to a 2.2 cubic foot family model, and the controls and styling carry across the range. The family look is easy to recognize: a gray interior, a white LED display and a carousel tray.
Choosing within the ladder is mostly about cavity size, wattage and whether the oven carries inverter or sensor technology. This guide lines up six models so you can see what each rung adds.

products.name: Sharp SMC1464KS 1.4 cu ft 1100W inverter microwave, stainless
products.description:
The SMC1464KS is the sweet spot of the Sharp line. An inverter circuit holds output steady at each power level, so a low setting really is low rather than a series of full-power pulses. That keeps edges from cooking while the center of a frozen portion is still icy.

A 1.4 cubic foot cavity and a 12.4 inch carousel handle a dinner plate easily, and ten power levels with two-stage cooking let you chain a defrost step into a heating step. A gray interior and white LED display improve readability, and LED lighting lets you see the food. Compared with the SMC1162KS, you gain inverter power and 0.3 cubic feet.

Care is simple. Wipe the interior while warm, wash the tray and keep the rear vent clear. The stainless front shows fingerprints, so keep a soft cloth nearby. For most kitchens, this is the Sharp to buy. The 12.4 inch tray matches the size most owners already have in plates and bowls.
products.bestFor: Kitchens that defrost and reheat often and want inverter power at a family size.
pros: Inverter holds steady power at every level
1.4 cu ft cavity with a 12.4 in carousel
Two-stage cooking chains defrost and heat
Gray interior and LED lighting aid visibility
cons: Costs more than non-inverter Sharp models

products.name: Sharp SMC0962KS 0.9 cu ft 900W stainless microwave with 10.6 in carousel
products.description:
This is the compact stainless Sharp, and it keeps the family features in a smaller box. A 900 watt output, a 0.9 cubic foot cavity and a 10.6 inch carousel suit apartments and small kitchens. The cooking platform design and gray interior make food easy to see.

Ten power levels and two-stage cooking give more control than most compact ovens at this size. The tray is a little wider than the 10 inch tray on the 0.7 cubic foot model, so a dinner plate sits more comfortably. Compared with the SMC1162KS, you save counter space and lose 100 watts and 0.2 cubic feet.

The oven has no inverter, so low settings pulse. Give the interior a wipe and keep vents clear. It is the sensible pick for a small kitchen that wants Sharp's controls without the cost of a larger model. Because the cavity is small, plan on cooking one dish at a time and stirring halfway. That habit does more for even heating than any extra feature.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that want the Sharp control layout in a compact cabinet.
pros: Two-stage cooking at a compact size
Lower cost than the 1.1 cu ft model
cons: No inverter, so low settings pulse

products.name: Sharp SMC0760KB 0.7 cu ft 700W black microwave with 10 in carousel
products.description:
This is the smallest Sharp in the guide. A 0.7 cubic foot cavity, 700 watts and a 10 inch carousel suit a dorm shelf, an office or a studio. It comes in black or white, with the family gray interior, white LED display and LED lighting.

Ten power levels with two-stage cooking are unusual in a 700 watt oven, and they help because slow ovens benefit from programmed thaw-then-heat steps. A 10 inch tray fits small plates and bowls but not a wide dinner plate. Compared with the SMC0962KS, you lose 200 watts and a bit of cavity.

The low wattage means longer cook times, so add time to package directions. Wipe down the interior and keep the vent clear. It suits students and small offices that want a known brand. Check housing or office rules about appliance wattage before you buy. Its low draw is an advantage on shared circuits.
products.bestFor: Dorms and offices that want a tiny Sharp with staged cooking.
pros: Two-stage cooking in a 700 W oven
cons: 700 W is slow for full plates

products.name: Sharp SMC1162KS 1.1 cu ft 1000W stainless microwave with carousel
products.description:
The SMC1162KS is the plain mid-size Sharp. A 1.1 cubic foot cavity, 1000 watts and a 12.4 inch carousel cover everyday cooking, and ten power levels with two-stage cooking add control. Popcorn presets are certified for a well-known brand of bags.

Without an inverter, low settings pulse, so defrosting needs more attention than on the SMC1464KS. The cabinet is a modest size, and the same oven comes in black as the SMC1161KB. Compared with the SMC0962KS, it adds 100 watts and a larger tray.

Wipe down the interior and wash the tray. It is a straightforward pick for a household that wants Sharp's reputation at a mid price and has no need for an inverter. The 1000 watt output matches most package directions, so you will rarely adjust times. The black twin, the SMC1161KB, offers the same hardware if the finish suits your counter better.
products.bestFor: Households that want a standard mid-size Sharp without paying for an inverter.
cons: No inverter, so low settings pulse

products.name: Sharp SMC1662KS 1.6 cu ft 1100W sensor microwave with 13.6 in carousel
products.description:
The SMC1662KS adds Sensor Cook to a family-sized 1.6 cubic foot cavity. Six presets use steam sensing to set time and power, and a blue LED display looks sharp on the stainless front. The removable 13.6 inch carousel is wide enough for a pizza and large platters.

Output is 1100 watts, which cooks large portions quickly. It does not carry an inverter, so low settings still pulse. Compared with the SMC1464KS, you gain a larger cavity and a sensor and lose inverter steadiness.

The big tray is awkward to wash in a small sink. Take a cloth to the interior after steamy foods so the sensor stays accurate. It suits families who reheat varied plates and want automatic timing. A pizza fits whole on the big tray, which is its everyday party trick. Compared with the SMC2266KS, it is less costly and easier to place on a standard counter.
products.bestFor: Families that reheat varied plates and want a large tray and a sensor.
pros: 1.6 cu ft cavity and 13.6 in tray
Blue LED display is easy to read
cons: Large tray is awkward to wash

products.name: Sharp SMC2266KS 2.2 cu ft 1200W inverter microwave with 16.5 in carousel
products.description:
The SMC2266KS is the biggest Sharp in the guide. A 2.2 cubic foot cavity, a 16.5 inch carousel and 1200 watts give room for platters and casseroles. An inverter keeps low settings steady, which matters more in a large cavity where cold spots are easier to produce.

Ten power levels and two-stage cooking give flexible control, and a gray interior with white LED display and lighting makes the cabinet easy to read. This is a big machine, so it needs a deep counter and a few inches of clearance. Compared with the SMC1464KS, you gain 0.8 cubic feet and a bigger tray.

Wiping the corners of a large cavity takes a while. The heavy tray is a two-handed job to wash. It is the right pick for large households and anyone who cooks for gatherings. Plan the counter before buying, because the door needs room to swing. A shallow shelf is the usual reason big ovens go back.
products.bestFor: Large households and gatherings that need a very big inverter cavity.
pros: 2.2 cu ft cavity with 16.5 in tray

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Sharp range steps from 0.7 to 2.2 cubic feet: 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.4, 1.6 and 2.2. Each step adds a little more tray width, from 10 inches to 16.5 inches. Pick the smallest cavity that fits your widest plate and your counter, since extra volume costs money and shelf space. A household of one or two rarely needs more than 1.1 cubic feet. Larger cabinets also weigh more and need deeper shelves, which is easy to forget when comparing numbers on a screen. Measure the counter first and treat the cavity as the last decision.

Only the SMC1464KS and SMC2266KS list inverter technology. The others pulse the magnetron on low settings. If you defrost or melt, an inverter gives more even results. For full-power reheating the difference is small, so do not pay for it if you rarely use low power. A simple test is whether you have ever scorched the edge of a thawed portion in an older oven. If you have, the inverter will earn its cost within months.

The SMC1662KS lists Sensor Cook with six presets that read steam to set time and power. It helps with varied portions but can be fooled by covered dishes. The others rely on you to set time. A sensor is helpful for a household with several cooks. Wipe the cavity dry between cycles, because leftover steam skews the next reading. Use a fixed timer for dense foods that the sensor reads poorly.

The range runs 700, 900, 1000, 1100 and 1200 watts. A 1100 or 1200 watt oven cooks noticeably faster than a 700 watt one on a full plate. Small portions can overshoot in a high-wattage oven, so use shorter intervals. Package directions assume 1000 to 1200 watts, so a 700 or 900 watt oven needs extra time. Start with the printed minimum and add short bursts.

All six models list ten power levels with two-stage cooking. It lets you chain a defrost step and a heat step, which helps especially at lower wattages. Learn the sequence once and it saves attention every time. A typical routine is a few minutes at a low level followed by a short blast at full power. Write the sequence on a sticky note until it becomes habit.

The family look uses a gray interior, white LED display and LED lighting, with stainless or black exteriors. A gray interior makes food easier to see, and stainless shows fingerprints. Choose the finish that suits your kitchen, since cooking performance is the same. Black hides fingerprints but shows dust, while stainless does the opposite. A white LED display reads clearly in both finishes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brand purity
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only Sharp-branded countertop ovens and left out drawer and over-the-range models. That left six distinct machines. Black and stainless variants of one model were counted once.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power delivery
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for inverter designs. The SMC1464KS and SMC2266KS list it, and the others pulse. Defrost quality weighted this heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and tray
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cubic feet and carousel widths. The range runs from 0.7 cu ft with a 10 in tray to 2.2 cu ft with a 16.5 in tray. Plate fit weighed above volume.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cooking aids
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted sensors, two-stage cooking and presets. The SMC1662KS has Sensor Cook, and all six have two-stage cooking. Aids that reduce guesswork scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership signals
howWeEvaluated.description: Reported trouble from owners centers on touch pads, latches and magnetrons as wear points. A shared design across the range makes manuals and parts easier to find.

cards.label: Inverter
cards.text: The SMC1464KS and SMC2266KS hold steady output, so low settings are gentle. This suits defrosting and melting. It costs more.

cards.label: Standard
cards.text: The SMC0760KB, SMC0962KS, SMC1162KS and SMC1662KS pulse the magnetron at low levels. Full-power reheating is unaffected. Defrosting needs more care.

howToChoose.note: Pick an inverter model if you defrost. Pick a standard model if you only reheat.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A small kitchen needs a narrow body, a tray that fits a plate and moderate power. A 0.7 to 0.9 cu ft oven suits most small counters.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SMC0962KS gives the best balance with a 10.6 in tray and 900 W. The SMC0760KB is smaller still.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You defrost often or cook for a crowd. The SMC1464KS and SMC2266KS earn their cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly reheat and warm drinks. The SMC0962KS covers the basics.

maintenance.why: Splatter absorbs energy and bakes on. Wipe while warm.
Grease on the tray smokes when heated. Dry it fully.
Food film stops the door closing. Use mild soap.
Blocked vents trap heat and shorten magnetron life. Vacuum dust.
Grease dulls the LED panel. Use a dry microfiber cloth.

faq.q: Which Sharp microwave size should I buy?
faq.a: A 1.1 to 1.4 cubic foot model suits most kitchens. Choose 0.7 to 0.9 for small spaces and 1.6 to 2.2 for large households. Measure counter and plates first. A tape measure beats a spec sheet, because door swing and plug position also decide where an oven can sit. Leave space behind for airflow.

faq.q: Is the Sharp inverter worth it?
faq.a: If you defrost and melt often, yes. The SMC1464KS and SMC2266KS keep power steady at low settings. For plain reheating, a standard model is enough.
The SMC1662KS lists Sensor Cook with six presets. The others rely on time and power. Sensors help with varied portions.
It lets you set two power or time steps in sequence, such as defrost then cook. All six models list it. It saves attention on frozen foods.

faq.q: Are black and stainless models the same?
faq.a: The same model often comes in both finishes, like the SMC1161KB and SMC1162KS. Cooking performance matches. Choose by kitchen style, and confirm the full model number on the listing before you order. Black and stainless versions sometimes differ in price by a noticeable margin even though the hardware matches.

faq.q: How long do Sharp microwaves last?
faq.a: Realistic lifespan estimates run to several years, with touch pads, latches and magnetrons as common failures. Clean seals and good ventilation help, and so does avoiding empty runs. Treat the oven as a replaceable appliance and keep the receipt for the warranty period.
